theory: A tree is a hierarchical data structure consisting of nodes connected by edges, with a single root node at the top. Each node can have zero or more child nodes, forming a parent-child relationship. Binary trees limit each node to at most two children. Binary Search Trees (BSTs) maintain a sorted order where left children are smaller and right children are larger, enabling efficient searching and sorting. Trees are the foundation for databases, file systems, and many algorithms.
